ops.title: NSFileProviderManager.add propagates isHidden to existing domains — no remove+re-add retrofit needed
ops.body:
Proven on-machine 2026-07-14 (yasyf's primary Mac, macOS 25.5.0): after upgrading CCPoolStatus.app to a build whose `register()` sets `NSFileProviderDomain.isHidden = true` (first shipped v0.52.1) and restarting the daemon, ALL 12 pre-existing FP domains vanished from Finder's Locations sidebar — only one (acct-08) had been explicitly `ccp fp repair`ed. The daemon's reconcile re-register (fusekit `OpRegister`, an "idempotent" `NSFileProviderManager.add`) crossed into the new app's `register()` and the add() **updated the existing domains' properties in place**, contrary to the natural reading of the fusekit doc comment ("idempotent if already registered" ≠ no-op: Apple's add() updates a domain with the same identifier).

Consequences:
- Domain-property changes (isHidden, displayName) reach existing installs via plain upgrade + daemon restart; `ccp fp repair` is only needed for wedged replica state, not property retrofits.
- The retrofit is non-disruptive: no open-FD breakage, ~47 live sessions untouched, domains stay registered (`fileproviderctl dump` still lists all 12) — hidden, not removed.
- On-machine spike verdict for the v0.52.1 fix: `isHidden` DOES remove the entry from Finder's Locations sidebar (public API, macOS 11+; was only compile-verified at ship time).

Operational gotcha hit on the way: `ccp service install` reported "✓ Started the daemon" but left the old v0.53.0 daemon running (and `ccp status --json`'s top-level `version` field reflected the CLI writing the snapshot, not the daemon). `brew services restart cc-pool` is the reliable restart; `ccp fp repair`'s health-version check is the reliable daemon-version probe.
